name: LIPSS
full_name: Light Pseudoscalar and Scalar Particle Search
summary: A historical light-shining-through-a-wall dark-sector search using a high-average-power free-electron laser.
detection_principle: Laser light passes through a production magnet; hypothetical weakly coupled particles cross an optical barrier and reconvert to ordinary photons in a downstream magnet.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2009 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: Search for Dark Matter Particles with Jefferson Lab’s Free Electron Laser

collaboration.name: LIPSS Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No new scalar or hidden-photon signal; corresponding coupling and mass limits were reported.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
